system:
You are a computational cancer biologist searching CRISPR screen data for selective genetic dependencies: genes that cancer cells with a particular alteration (the biomarker) need more than other cancer cells do. Such genes are candidate drug targets with a built-in patient-selection strategy.

Work like a careful scientist:
1. Plan first with write_plan, and revise it as you learn.
2. Survey the data (genome_wide_top, scan_biomarker, scan_target) to generate candidate hypotheses.
3. Be sceptical before you believe a signal. Use inspect_association to check whether it is driven by one lineage or a disease subtype hiding inside a lineage, and whether the effect is large enough to matter. Ask whether the biology makes sense (paralog buffering, pathway dependence, oncogene addiction). A broadly essential target may lack a therapeutic window.
4. Check the literature with search_pubmed before registering, and judge novelty honestly.
5. Register only your best hypotheses (register_hypothesis). Registration is final and must come before replication. You have 5 replications, each of which must pass one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad cell lines and independent Sanger screens.
6. Report honestly with submit_findings. A hypothesis is replicated only if replicate() said so. Negative results are results. Never let what you remember from the literature override what the data show.

You have at most 30 model turns. Batch independent tool calls in one turn.

input.mechanism: RB1 loss frees activator E2Fs; RB1-null cells become addicted to unrestrained E2F3-driven S-phase transcription (E2F3 is highly expressed in RB1-mutant lines), consistent across lung, bladder, uterus, CNS, bone.

DYRK1A promotes quiescence via DREAM/LIN52 and cyclin D degradation; in RB1-null cells the residual cell-cycle control relies on DYRK1A-dependent p130/DREAM balance or DYRK1A supports splicing/transcription needed for E2F-driven proliferation. Effect consistent across lineages (-0.2 to -0.39).
FANCM remodels stalled forks and channels them away from break-induced repair; without BRCA1-mediated resection/HR, FANCM loss causes unresolved replication stress and lethality.

Constitutive NRF2 activity in KEAP1-mutant cells rewires NADPH and lipid metabolism; these cells rely on de novo fatty acid synthesis (FASN) for membrane lipids/redox buffering, creating a FASN dependency (FASN inhibitors e.g. TVB-2640 exist).

NF2/Merlin loss perturbs mitotic spindle/centrosome function and YAP-driven proliferation; such cells may depend on p31comet (MAD2L1BP)-TRIP13 mediated spindle checkpoint silencing to exit mitosis (TRIP13 also ranks second).

input.summary: I surveyed loss-of-function biomarkers (LOSS and damaging MUT). The strongest LOSS signals were mostly paralog pairs or markers of lymphoid and myeloma subtypes (for example the CYB561A3 and MEF2B hits), so I set them aside. I registered five tumour-suppressor hypotheses and replicated all five, using up the budget of five; three passed. The clearest hit is RB1 mutation → E2F3, which was strong in both held-out Broad lines and Sanger screens. The second, RB1 → DYRK1A, is a candidate I found no prior literature for; it was strong in held-out Broad lines but only just passed in Sanger (p=0.007, small effect). The third, BRCA1 → FANCM, matches recent preprints. KEAP1 → FASN and NF2 → MAD2L1BP did not replicate. My Python environment failed to load, so all analysis used the built-in scan and inspect tools.

findings.claim: Cancer lines with damaging RB1 mutations depend selectively on the activator E2F3 in every lineage checked (held-out Broad t=-10.3, Sanger t=-6.9).

RB1-mutant lines depend more on the kinase DYRK1A, which is a drug target. The effect is moderate and consistent across lineages but small in Sanger screens (beta -0.17, p=0.007), so it needs more validation.

BRCA1-mutant lines depend selectively on the fork-remodeling helicase FANCM. Few lines carry the mutation (6 held-out, 8 Sanger), but it passed in both datasets, and recent preprints report the same pair.
The discovery-set FASN dependency in KEAP1-mutant (mostly NSCLC) lines did not replicate: held-out Broad p=0.04, and no effect in Sanger.
The link between NF2 mutation and MAD2L1BP (p31comet) dependency was not reproduced in either held-out dataset.
